t: Vijayalaya founded the Chola Empire in 848, and the Cholas held peninsular India south of the Tungabhadra River as one state between 907 and 1215.
Rajendra I reached the Ganges, built a new capital called Gangaikonda Cholapuram, and in 1025 launched naval raids on the ports of Srivijaya.
The empire declined after Kulothunga Chola III's defeat by Maravarman Sundara Pandiyan II in 1215–16 and ceased to exist by 1279, absorbed by the Pandyan empire.
dyk: According to the Malay chronicle Sejarah Melayu, the rulers of the Malacca sultanate claimed descent from the kings of the Chola empire.
ev: Aditya I defeats the Pallava and Pandyan dynasties, capturing Tondaimandalam and Kongu Nadu
The Cholas send the first of three diplomatic missions to China
Rajendra Chola I launches naval raids on the ports of Srivijaya
Kulothunga Chola I takes the throne after Athirajendra Chola's assassination, beginning the Later Chola dynasty
The Cholas under Kulothunga Chola III help the Hoysalas defeat the Western Chalukyas
Kulothunga Chola III is defeated by Maravarman Sundara Pandiyan II
The Chola state ceases to exist, absorbed by the Pandyan empire

f.capital: Thanjavur, then Gangaikonda Cholapuram (built by Rajendra I); Urayur and Kaveripattinam were the early Cholas' capitals
f.founder: Vijayalaya, a descendant of the Early Cholas
f.predecessor: Pallava and Pandyan dynasties; the Early Cholas of the Sangam literature
